findings.title: Commit points are checkbox tasks, not plain `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description: All ten commit points (2C, 3C, 5C, 6C, 8C, 9C, 11C, 13C, 14C, 15C) are written as `- [ ] **Task nC: Commit** — …`. A commit checkbox can only be ticked after the commit it describes, which leaves a dirty tree or forces a check-off-only commit. Convert each to a plain `**Commit**: <message>` line under the preceding task. Their placement is fine: each sits after a tested group. Task 15C (line 269) commits only walkthrough notes; fold it into 14C or the last defect-fix commit.

findings.title: Renderer behaviour for three outcome kinds is unspecified and untested
findings.description: The slice's Technical Requirements ask for `renderAdoptionFacts` tests on "every outcome". Task 8 requires an exhaustive switch on `outcome.kind`, but Task 8T covers only brownfield, adoption-in-progress and `NOT_EVALUATED`. Task 8 never says what the outcome bullet reads for `greenfield`, `already-planned` or `adoption-closed`, so the implementer has to invent that text. Add one line to Task 8 stating the text (or that these kinds throw as unreachable), and a matching case each in 8T.

findings.title: Byte-identical walkthrough step does not say where each build runs
findings.description: This step is the only coverage of the Integration Requirement "planned projects build byte-identical prompts before and after". "A temporary `git worktree add` of `main`, built there" can be read as running `cfl build` inside the temp worktree. I did not check how `cf` resolves a project from an unregistered path, but that reading risks a failed build or a diff caused by the path rather than the slice. State it explicitly: compile the CLI in the temp worktree, then run both the main-built and slice-built `dist/index.js build` from the same registered checkout directory.

findings.title: History `unknown` reason will carry gitExec's full message
findings.description: Task 5 sets `reason` to the error message. `gitExec` wraps that as `git <args> failed in <cwd>: …` and passes it through `withNetworkErrorHint`, whose patterns match "timed out after Ns". The Adoption Facts history bullet may therefore include an absolute path and a network hint, not the design's short "git timed out after 5s". Task 5T's `contains 'timed out'` assertion still passes; decide whether Task 5 should trim the reason.

findings.title: `context_build` error result and CLI non-zero exit have no new automated test
findings.description:
No task adds a test for the criterion "`cf build` exits non-zero; `context_build` returns it as an error". Coverage is adequate without one:
- **Rethrow:** Task 10T asserts the integrator rejects on `AdoptionError`.
- **Pipeline:** Task 12 fixture 12 asserts the pipeline rejects on a guide without the profile.
- **MCP:** the existing catch turns any thrown error into `errorResult`, and `packages/mcp-server/tests/contextTools.test.ts:271` is an existing test named "returns isError on core generation failure".
- **CLI:** Task 15 walkthrough step 4 checks the exit code by hand.

findings.title: Functional success criteria all trace to tasks
Unit-test requirements, sequencing and test-with pattern
findings.description: Each implementation task (1–10) is followed directly by its test task, and Task 11 carries its own tests. Dependencies run in order: key and contracts, then facts, outcome, renderer, resolver, integrator, callers. The two import cycles (`ConfigKeys` ↔ `adoptionState`, `adoptionOutcome` ↔ `sourceVolume`) are handled explicitly. Other than the renderer gap above, the listed unit tests match the slice's Technical Requirements item by item.

findings.title: Caller update list matches the code
findings.description: The only source callers of `createContextPipeline` are `packages/cli/src/commands/build.ts:84` and `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/contextTools.ts:92`, both named in Task 11. The task's grep reaches every test caller: `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts`, `pipeline-integration.test.ts` and `build.integration.test.ts`. Every existing test file the tasks name exists, as does the README row for `workflow.permissiveness` (`README.md:388`).

findings.title: No scope creep; proportionality fits the slice
findings.description: Every task traces to a Development Approach step or a success criterion. The Task 6 pattern extraction is the task file's own answer to D6's "other read errors throw", not extra scope; the existing regex is already case-insensitive (`ArtifactIntrospector.ts:39`). Sixteen tasks in one file is proportionate to about ten new source files. No merge or push tasks are present.

findings.title: Performance target needs no load test
findings.description: D2 states the sub-second target and decides that "tests assert the caps, not timings". The target is not in the Success Criteria. Task 3T asserts both caps (early exit and `MAX_WALK_ENTRIES`), and the Context Summary records the reasoning, so no `tests/load/` or CI gating task is owed.
